subject: Subprocessor ownership clarification + export-control constraints
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acmepayments.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@acmepayments.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor roster + export-control constraints

Hi Evelyn,

As part of our procurement checklist, we need the most up-to-date list of Redwood subprocessors that will process Acme Payments data. In particular, our security team flagged two items we need clarified: 

- Which subprocessors (if any) have access to raw transaction payloads or PII?
- Do you have any subprocessors located or routing through jurisdictions outside the US that would be involved in processing Acme customer data?
- Are there any subprocessors that store persistent logs in a third country (specifically EU/APAC)?

We also need to confirm whether Redwood can commit to onshore-only processing for a subset of our environment (we can scope by tenant IDs) or if you rely on temporary transit through non-US regions for certain telemetry/observability partners.

Could you share the roster and a short note on export-control / cross-border exposure? If a DPA amendment is required to add constraints, please attach a draft.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior IT Procurement
Acme Payments
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster + export-control constraints

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear list. Attaching our current roster (redwood-subprocessor-roster-v2.xlsx) and a proposed DPA amendment template (dpa-amendment-draft.docx) that narrows processing location by tenant where feasible. Quick notes up front: 

- Access to raw transaction payloads / PII: only a small set of telemetry and observability subprocessors (names in sheet: TelemetryVendorA, MetricsFlow) receive obfuscated traces for performance diagnostics. No payment payloads are sent to analytics partners; those are strictly processed by our core serving layer which is onshore for dedicated tenants.
- Cross-border transit: we do route metrics and some aggregated telemetry through EU edge collectors in normal operation for performance; however we have an onshore-only option that pins routing to US edges for dedicated/enterprise tenants. That option is a configuration and incurs modest latency tradeoffs.
- Persistent logs: primary logs for customer data live in US regions for onshore-tenants. Aggregated ops logs may be stored in EU for compliance reasons with that partner — noted in the roster.

Action items proposed: 
1) I can toggle onshore routing for the tenant(s) you specify; please send the tenant IDs or production hostnames.
2) Marissa — can you review the attached DPA amendment and confirm whether the language on subprocessor restrictions and onshore routing is acceptable?
3) Karthik — can you confirm the operational steps and expected RTO/RPO when we change routing for a tenant (and whether any rolling restart is required)?

I'll await tenant IDs and Marissa's review.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-subprocessor-roster-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB), dpa-amendment-draft.docx (document, 24KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster + export-control constraints

Jordan / Evelyn — I reviewed the draft amendment. High-level feedback: 

- The onshore-only obligation can be included for the specified tenant IDs, but we should add a narrow exception for emergency failover (explicitly limited, with notification windows and audit logs).
- Suggest tightening the definition of "access to raw transaction payloads" so that it excludes telemetry/metrics that are purpose-limited and redacted. I added suggested wording (see tracked changes in attached draft).
- For export-control / cross-border language, add a requirement for Redwood to provide a quarterly attestation of routing and a one-off export-impact map on request.

Evelyn — once you confirm the operational feasibility with Karthik, I can finalize the amendment and circulate to Acme Legal.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data
Redwood Inference
Attachment: dpa-amendment-draft.docx (tracked-changes)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acmepayments.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster + export-control constraints

Thanks — this looks good. We can provide two tenant IDs for the onshore constraint: acct-prod-01 and acct-prod-02. A couple of quick asks before we proceed: 

- Can you confirm estimated latency delta if onshore routing is enforced? We need a number for the procurement risk sheet.
- Please send the redline DPA back to us (DocuSign link would be ideal).
- For the attestation cadence, quarterly certs are acceptable — please include a sample attestation format.

Marissa — if the language you suggested is in the redline, Acme Legal is likely to approve quickly. Evelyn/Karthik, let us know the ETA for the change (we're aiming for the configuration to be active before the July pilot).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Jordan
Procurement
Acme Payments
